stem.en: Each wave carries sand up a beach and then runs back. Why can the beach still build up?

text.en: The sand is too heavy for waves to move at all.

feedback.en: Waves do move sand. That is how a beach forms.

text.en: The backwash is weaker, so some sand stays.

feedback.en: Right. Part of the water sinks in, so less runs back.

text.en: The backwash carries more sand than the swash.

feedback.en: If that were always so, the beach would shrink.

text.en: Waves stop moving when they reach the beach.

feedback.en: Water keeps running up and back on every wave.

explanation.en: The swash carries sand up the beach. Part of its water soaks into the sand, so the backwash is weaker and leaves some sand behind.

hints.en: Compare the water going up with the water coming back.
